summary: Civilian Conservation Corps fire tower on Dick Ridge in Walker County, Georgia, built in 1941 and dismantled in 1960. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 60-foot tower on treated wooden poles with an 8 by 8 foot wooden cab and a catwalk with handrails
facts.status_note: Dismantled in 1960 according to the Armuchee Ranger District history; no source describes the site now

access.note: The ridge is in the Chattahoochee National Forest and a foot-only trail loops around it. No source describes access to the old tower site.

visit.trail_note: Chickamauga Creek Trail, a 6.2-mile loop designated for foot travel only, starts at the end of Ponder Creek Road and goes around Dick Ridge.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Armuchee Ranger District

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps

corrections.why: The forest-lookout page places Dick Ridge in Walker County, Chattahoochee National Forest. tnlandforms lists Whitfield. Not checked against a county boundary map.

notes_for_editor: Tower is gone (dismantled 1960), so the site-today line says no source describes it. County conflict: tnlandforms says Whitfield, the forest-lookout page and the Armuchee history place the ridge in Walker County; proposed correction needs a county-boundary check against the coordinates 34.72611, -85.14441. The interview's date for Copeland's move is loose ('Sometime in the early 50's'), so staffing as_of is approximate. The trail description is undated in the history; it may be out of date. Only one source family (the Armuchee history, quoted again on the forest-lookout page) covers this tower; NHLR and FFLA have no entry. Used 3 web searches. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the story now states Walker County from the forest-lookout page and discloses the tnlandforms Whitfield entry; the boundary check against 34.72611, -85.14441 is still open. The 'early 1950s' move is stated as loose.
